title: Permanence and separation for ind-quasi-affine morphisms
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Say $f$ has property $P$ if, for every affine open $U\subset Y$ and every quasi-compact open $K\subset f^{-1}(U)$, the induced morphism $K\to U$ is quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism]. Then (1) $P$ is preserved by arbitrary base change [def-pc-fibre-product]; (2) if $Y=\bigcup_i U_i$ is any affine open cover, $P(f)$ holds if and only if $P(f^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i)$ holds for every $i$; (3) if $Y$ is affine and $P(f)$ holds, every quasi-compact open of $X$ is a quasi-affine scheme (a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme), and $X$ is separated, hence quasi-separated [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism].

proof.text: First record two elementary translations. If $q:Q\to A$ has affine target and is quasi-affine, then $Q$ is quasi-affine by applying [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism] to the whole affine open $A$. A quasi-compact open $L$ of a quasi-affine scheme $Q$ is again quasi-affine: compose its open inclusion with an open embedding of $Q$ into an affine scheme; the image of $L$ is open and quasi-compact. Conversely, if $Q$ is quasi-affine and $A$ affine, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] and clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] make any $q:Q\to A$ quasi-compact. The inverse image of every affine open of $A$ is thus a quasi-compact open of $Q$, hence quasi-affine by the preceding argument, which is precisely the definition that $q$ is quasi-affine.

For clause (2), the forward implication is immediate: an affine open of $U_i$ is also an affine open of $Y$, and the corresponding inverse-image open and induced map are unchanged. For the converse, assume $P$ for each restriction to $U_i$. Fix an affine open $V\subseteq Y$ and a quasi-compact open $K\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$. The map $q:K\to V$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). Use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] to cover $V$ by affine opens $V_a$, each contained in some $U_{i(a)}$. Since $q$ is quasi-compact, $K_a=q^{-1}(V_a)$ is quasi-compact. It is open in $f^{-1}(U_{i(a)})$, so the hypothesis $P(f|_{U_{i(a)}})$ applied to the whole affine target $U_{i(a)}$ gives a quasi-affine map $K_a\to U_{i(a)}$. Step 1 makes $K_a$ a quasi-affine scheme. Apply [lem-a1-quasi-affine-target-locality] to $q$ and the affine cover $(V_a)$: $K\to V$ is quasi-affine. This proves $P(f)$. In particular, no intersection $V\cap U_i$ has been assumed affine.

source.place: Tag 0F1U, proof (3) implies (4), specialized to an affine cover

proof.text: For clause (1), let $g:T\to Y$ be arbitrary and put $X_T=X\times_YT$. Choose an affine open cover $(U_i)$ of $Y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], $T$ has an affine open cover $(V_b)$ with each $V_b\subseteq g^{-1}(U_{i(b)})$. Clause (2), already proved, reduces the assertion to $X\times_YV_b\to V_b$ for each $b$. Fix $b$ and a quasi-compact open $L\subseteq X\times_YV_b$. Its image under the first projection is a quasi-compact subset of $f^{-1}(U_{i(b)})$: pull any open covering of that image back to $L$ and take a finite subcover. Cover that image by affine opens contained in $f^{-1}(U_{i(b)})$, using the affine-open basis again, and retain finitely many. Their union is a quasi-compact open $W\subseteq f^{-1}(U_{i(b)})$ containing the image. The projection $L\to X$ factors through $W$, since a morphism whose image lies in an open subscheme restricts to it [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 0AP7, reduction to affine bases; finite affine enlargement of the projected quasi-compact open

proof.text: The hypothesis $P(f)$ makes $W\to U_{i(b)}$ quasi-affine. By [lem-trf-quasi-affine-base-change], its base change $W\times_{U_{i(b)}}V_b\to V_b$ is quasi-affine. Since $V_b$ is affine, its source is quasi-affine by Step 1. The inclusion of $W\times_{U_{i(b)}}V_b$ into $X\times_YV_b$ is an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Its image contains $L$, by construction of $W$, so $L$ is a quasi-compact open of that quasi-affine source. Step 1 makes $L$ quasi-affine. Now let $V'\subseteq V_b$ be any affine open and $L$ any quasi-compact open of the inverse image of $V'$; the argument above applies verbatim to $L$ (only $L\subseteq X\times_YV_b$ was used), so $L$ is a quasi-affine scheme, and the converse part of Step 1, with the affine target $V'$, makes $L\to V'$ quasi-affine. Thus $P(X\times_YV_b\to V_b)$ holds for every $b$; the reduction in Step 3 proves arbitrary base-change stability.

source.place: Tag 0AP7; explicit quasi-compact-open argument using ordinary quasi-affine base-change stability

proof.text: For clause (3), suppose $Y$ is affine. Apply $P(f)$ to $U=Y$: every quasi-compact open $K\subseteq X$ has quasi-affine map $K\to Y$, so Step 1 makes $K$ a quasi-affine scheme. In particular, for any two affine opens $A,B\subseteq X$, their union $W=A\cup B$ is quasi-compact: an open cover has finite subcovers on $A$ and on $B$. Hence $W$ is quasi-affine. By [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding], $W$ is separated, so its absolute diagonal is a closed immersion.

Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and $D=X\times_SX$. For every pair of affine opens $A,B$ of $X$, set $W=A\cup B$ as in Step 5. The two projection inverse images of $W$ are open in $D$; their intersection is the open subscheme $D_W=W\times_SW$, by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and the fibre-product universal property. These $D_W$ cover $D$: the projections of any point of $D$ belong to some affine opens $A$ and $B$, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The inverse image of $D_W$ under the absolute diagonal is $W$, and the restricted diagonal is exactly $\Delta_W$ (both components are the identity). It is a closed immersion by Step 5.

source.place: Tag 0AP6, separatedness paragraph; explicit open cover of the absolute diagonal target

proof.text: Check the closed-immersion definition [def-weil-closed-immersion] directly for $\Delta_X$ on the cover $(D_W)$. Its image is closed because its intersection with each $D_W$ is the closed image of $\Delta_W$. The diagonal is injective (its composite with the first projection is the identity). Its inverse onto the image is continuous, being the restriction of the first projection, so it is a homeomorphism onto this closed image. Finally, the structure-sheaf map is surjective: a section germ can be lifted locally in any $D_W$ containing the point, since the restricted map is that of the closed immersion $\Delta_W$; these are exactly the local lifts required for surjectivity of a map of sheaves. Thus $\Delta_X$ is a closed immersion and $X$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated] to $X\to S$ to conclude that $X$ is quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 0AP6, separatedness paragraph; direct closed-immersion check and separated implies quasi-separated

lean.statement: theorem indQuasiAffineProperty_permanence {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : T ⟶ Y), indQuasiAffineProperty f → indQuasiAffineProperty (Limits.pullback.snd f g)) ∧ (∀ {I : Type v} (U : I → Y.Opens), (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) → iSup U = ⊤ → (indQuasiAffineProperty f ↔ ∀ i, indQuasiAffineProperty (Limits.pullback.snd f (U i).ι))) ∧ (∀ (_hY : IsAffine Y), indQuasiAffineProperty f → (∀ (K : X.Opens), IsCompact (K : Set X) → K.toScheme.IsQuasiAffine) ∧ Scheme.IsSeparated X ∧ QuasiSeparatedSpace X)
lean.note: The helper predicate indQuasiAffineProperty is the exact P condition stated in the node; the theorem gives all three clauses. The pullback presentation is the canonical scheme model of the inverse image over an affine open.
